symptom: `alter workflow M.W { drop userTask1 path 1 }` (and the old `drop path 'Path 1' on userTask1`) deleted the user task's FIRST OUTCOME and printed "Altered workflow"; `drop path '' on X` deleted the last outcome/path. Measured on TestApp's Studio Pro-authored workflow.Workflow1: 'Good' of Good/Bad/Ugly gone, project still loads, check clean
cause: DropPath (wfmutator and the MCP mutator) matched "Path N" against the index of whatever Outcomes list the resolved activity had, never checking it was a parallel split; the insert ops' kind check (#415) lived only in the executor, which reads the STORED workflow, and it deliberately skipped the drops because a drop cannot write a wrong type — but it can address the wrong member
fix: backend.CheckWorkflowMemberList (per storage $Type, the member lists the document declares) guards every member op in both mutators; backend.ParallelPathIndex refuses an empty/unnumbered caption and an out-of-range number; validateAlterWorkflowActivityKinds refuses drop path on a non-split at check time; `drop X boundary event` among several is refused under mdl 1 / warns MDL-V1-BOUNDARYDROP under mdl 0
insight: A drop cannot corrupt the TYPE of a list, which is why #415's guard left drops out — but an index-addressed drop on a list of another kind silently removes real content. Old unit fixtures built the split and decision as Workflows$UserTask, so the tests could never have seen it; the guard made those fixtures fail first
